result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers explain the real problem well: 12 tiles were lit at once, so the real outage didn't stand out, and brighter red would just make all 12 louder. B gives more specific fixes (showing values instead of just colours, a 'what's breaking now' strip, flagging tiles that stop updating) and a sharper pre-meeting check. However, it cites a 'well-documented' effect without a source, calls the outage day 'a normal day', and is longer with more technical terms. A is shorter, sticks to the user's numbers and is easier for a non-technical director to follow, so it edges ahead. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers explain clearly that 12 lit tiles made the real outage hard to spot. Both give concrete fixes: make red rare, rank the tiles, and page someone for critical alerts. B is slightly better for this audience because its tips on how to persuade the director are more useful (start by agreeing with his instinct, don't call the other 11 tiles meaningless) and it gives a measurable goal and a practice drill. A has more useful pre-meeting checks but includes some more technical items. A also says the effect is 'well-documented' without naming any source.
